challengeFindings.title: `/bkit-ship` on a branch whose open PR conflicts with dev dies at its Step 2 / Step 3 publish push, so it never reaches the Step 4 merge that would fix the conflict

A PR that conflicts on GitHub only in a `merge=union` ledger (`docs/knowledge.jsonl`, `.bkit/stats.jsonl`, `status.jsonl` ...) passes the check, because `git merge-tree` applies the work tree's `.gitattributes` union driver and GitHub does not, so CI still never starts

In a single-branch clone (fetch refspec covers only the branch, common for cloud agents), `git fetch origin dev` succeeds without creating `refs/remotes/origin/dev`, `git merge-tree` exits 1 with "not something we can merge", and the hook BLOCKS the push with an empty conflicting-files list

A consumer whose older hook lacks `PUSH_BRANCH_SHA` in its stdin loop follows the `pre-push-pr-conflict` tip, pastes the two blocks, and gets a check that silently never runs, while the tip stops firing because `merge-tree` is now present

An outside attacker opens a fork PR whose head branch has the same name as a bkit feature branch, and the pre-push hook trial-merges the victim's push against the attacker's chosen base, blocking it and printing a Fix that tells the agent to merge that base

challengeFindings.title: A sibling PR merges into `dev` while `/bkit-ship` runs Steps 5-7 and appends to a shared `merge=union` ledger; ship's Step 8 `[skip ci]` bookkeeping push (or the Step 10 regenerate push) is then BLOCKED by the PR conflict check and ship takes the Failure Path, instead of reaching the Step 10 merge gate whose exit 19 (stale base) routes back to Step 3 / Step 4 integration

`/bkit-debug` remediates a red PR, and during the run `dev` gains a ledger row that collides with the debug branch's own `docs/failures.jsonl` / `docs/knowledge.jsonl` appends; the Step 9 remediation push is BLOCKED, debug takes the Failure Path, and its handover never pushes onto a branch with an open PR, so the fix commits exist only in the local worktree and are lost with a cloud sandbox

A cloud agent in a shallow (`--depth=1`) clone pushes its PR branch; the hook's base fetch downloads the whole history of the base branch, and `git merge-tree` then refuses with refusing to merge unrelated histories (exit 128), so the check costs a full-history download and still only warns, on every push from that sandbox

A contributor working from a fork pushes a `[skip ci]` HEAD onto the branch of their own open PR to the upstream repo; the new `isCrossRepository | not` filter drops their PR, so the CI-suppressor guard, which blocked this push before the change, now allows it and the PR's checks stay green without testing the pushed code

On a machine or CI runner without `jq`, the stub `gh` in `fork PR with the same head branch name → ignored, gates run` exits 127 with no output; the hook reads that as a failed lookup, warns and runs the gates, so the test passes whatever the hook's fork filter does

A collaborator creates a base branch named `base;id` (a valid ref name), retargets the PR to it, and the hook's BLOCKED Fix line prints `git fetch origin base;id && git merge origin/base;id`, which an agent pasting the printed fix runs as `id`

challengeFindings.title: A contributor working from a fork pushes a `[skip ci]` HEAD onto the branch of their own open PR to the upstream repo; the lookup's `isCrossRepository | not` filter drops their PR, so the CI-suppressor guard, which blocked this push before the change, now allows it and the PR's checks stay green without testing the pushed code

`/bkit-plan` or `/bkit-design` re-runs on a feature branch that already has an open PR, and `dev` has gained a row in a `merge=union` ledger that the branch also appended to; the summary push is BLOCKED by the PR conflict check, the run takes the Failure Path, and the handover never pushes onto a branch with an open PR, so the summary commits exist only in the local worktree

In a repo with submodules, the base fetch follows git's default `fetch.recurseSubmodules=on-demand` and also fetches every submodule whose pointer the new base commits move; a slow or unreachable submodule remote stalls the push before the gates or fails the fetch, so the check is skipped with `could not fetch '<base>' from origin` although the base itself was fetched

A branch has two open same-repo PRs, one to `main` that merges cleanly and an older one to `dev` that conflicts; the lookup keeps only `.[0]`, the newest PR, so the hook trial-merges against `main`, lets the push through, and the `dev` PR's CI never starts

An outside attacker forks the repo, names a branch after the victim's feature branch and opens 30 PRs from it to 30 different base branches; `gh pr list --head` returns only the newest 30 PRs, the hook's new same-repo filter then finds none, and the hook treats the branch as having no open PR, so a `[skip ci]` code head passes the CI-suppressor guard and the conflict check is skipped with no message

A collaborator renames a file the victim's branch edits to a name holding a terminal escape sequence (for example `x<ESC>[2Jy.txt`) on the PR's base; git prints the conflicting path quoted as `"x\033[2Jy.txt"`, but the hook's `echo "$PR_MERGE_OUT"` under `sh` (macOS bash 3.2 in POSIX mode, Debian / Ubuntu dash) turns `\033` back into a raw ESC byte, so the pusher's terminal runs the sequence
